title: Phoenix, AZ real estate with a West Valley native
seoTitle: Phoenix AZ Homes and Neighborhoods | Teigh Wade REALTOR®
description: Phoenix real estate with Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, a Phoenix-born agent: urban villages, historic districts, Maryvale, Laveen, freeways, APS and SRP, and tips.
summary: Phoenix is Arizona's capital and the county seat of Maricopa County, incorporated in 1881. The city is organized into 15 urban villages, from historic districts such as Willo and Encanto-Palmcroft to west-side villages like Maryvale, Laveen and Estrella. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, was born in Phoenix and helps clients buy and sell across the city.

sections.html:
Phoenix incorporated as a city on February 25, 1881, and today it is both the state capital and the seat of Maricopa County. It is the center of a metro area that includes every West Valley city on this site. Teigh Wade was born here before spending most of her life in the West Valley, so Phoenix is the city she grew up around.

Because Phoenix is so large, the city divides itself into 15 urban villages for planning, each with its own character. Villages on the west and south sides include Maryvale, Estrella and Laveen. Deer Valley and North Gateway cover much of the north. Central Phoenix holds downtown, the oldest neighborhoods and most of the city's historic districts.

Phoenix has 36 residential historic districts protected by Historic Preservation overlay zoning. Among the best known are Willo, Encanto-Palmcroft, F.Q. Story, Roosevelt, Coronado, Country Club Park, Woodland and Windsor Square. Homes in these areas range from early 20th-century bungalows and period revival houses to mid-century designs, and many sit on tree-lined streets close to downtown.

Buying in a historic district comes with extra considerations. Exterior changes may need review under the city's historic preservation rules, and older systems, from wiring to sewer lines, deserve careful inspection. Teigh can help you line up the right questions before you write an offer.

sections.h2: West Phoenix: Maryvale, Estrella and Laveen
sections.html:
Maryvale

Maryvale was one of the first large planned communities in the Valley. Developer John F. Long began selling homes there by 1954 and named the community after his wife, Mary. It lies on the city's west side, roughly southwest of Grand Avenue, west of I-17 and north of I-10. Much of its housing is mid-century block ranch homes. The ballpark at 51st Avenue and Indian School Road, which opened as Maryvale Baseball Park, is the spring training home of the Milwaukee Brewers.

Estrella

Estrella Village covers part of southwest Phoenix. Its homes range across several decades, so check the build year and HOA status of each subdivision you tour.

Laveen

Laveen Village lies southwest of downtown, west of South Mountain Park. It includes newer subdivisions as well as some larger-lot properties, and the Laveen Elementary School District is one of Phoenix Union's partner districts.

• Historic homes in central Phoenix, often with no HOA but with historic preservation rules.
  • Mid-century ranch homes in large postwar neighborhoods such as Maryvale.
  • Master-planned subdivisions from the 1990s onward on the city's edges, usually with HOAs.
  • Condos, townhomes and high-rise living concentrated downtown and along major corridors.
  • Larger-lot and horse properties in parts of the outer villages, where zoning allows.

With so much variety, Phoenix home values depend heavily on the village, the street, the age of the home and its condition. Teigh prepares a comparative market analysis instead of quoting citywide figures.

Phoenix has the most extensive freeway network in the state. Interstate 10 runs east-west through downtown, and Interstate 17 runs north toward Flagstaff. Loop 101 and Loop 202 circle much of the metro area, State Route 51 runs north from downtown, and Loop 303 crosses the far north of the city near I-17. Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport sits just east of downtown, and Valley Metro operates light rail and bus routes.

1. Utilities. Phoenix is served by both APS and SRP for electricity, and their service areas overlap across the metro. Confirm the provider for the specific address, since rate plans differ.
  2. HOA status. Older neighborhoods often have no HOA; newer subdivisions and condos usually do. Read the CC&Rs and confirm dues and fees at closing.
  3. Historic rules. In a historic district, ask how the overlay affects exterior changes before you plan a remodel.
  4. Older home systems. On mid-century homes, look at the electrical panel, plumbing, sewer line and roof, and ask about irrigation if the lot is flood irrigated.
  5. Solar and pools. Confirm solar ownership and get a pool inspection.
  6. Animal and lot zoning. If you want horses or extra structures, verify the zoning before you make an offer.

Teigh's buying services carry you from pre-approval referrals to the closing table.

Phoenix is served by many school districts. Phoenix Union High School District covers much of the city's older core and receives students from partner elementary districts including Alhambra, Balsz, Cartwright, Creighton, Isaac, Laveen, Madison, Murphy, Osborn, Phoenix Elementary, Riverside, Roosevelt and Wilson. Other parts of the city are served by different unified and high school districts, so the district for a home depends entirely on its location. Check with the district before you rely on any school assignment.

A few landmarks show up in almost every Phoenix conversation: South Mountain Park, Papago Park with its Hole in the Rock, the Desert Botanical Garden, downtown's sports and arts venues, and Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. On the west side, the Milwaukee Brewers' spring training ballpark brings Cactus League games to Maryvale every year.

Phoenix buyers have a huge range of choices, so a listing needs to stand out in its own neighborhood. Expect questions about the roof, AC, electrical and plumbing updates, sewer line, solar, HOA dues and, in historic districts, what has been restored or replaced. Gathering receipts and permits for past work helps you answer quickly.

Teigh includes staging help for her listing clients and offers staging consultations and full staging with her own furniture; the home staging services page has the details. She builds a pricing plan around comparable sales in your village and never promises a price or a timeline.

Teigh Wade is a Phoenix-born REALTOR® with HomeSmart Elite Group, HomeSmart, the brokerage based in Phoenix. She works all over the Valley and offers mobile consultations, so she will come to you whether you are in Maryvale, Laveen or a central historic district.

faqs.a: Phoenix incorporated as a city on February 25, 1881. It is Arizona's state capital and the county seat of Maricopa County, and it sits at the center of a metro area that includes Glendale, Peoria, Surprise, Goodyear, Buckeye and the rest of the West Valley.

Phoenix divides itself into 15 urban villages for planning purposes. Each village has its own planning committee and character. Examples include Maryvale, Estrella and Laveen on the west and south sides, Deer Valley and North Gateway in the north, and the central villages around downtown.

faqs.q: Does Phoenix have APS or SRP?
faqs.a: Both. Arizona Public Service (APS) and Salt River Project (SRP) each serve parts of Phoenix, and their service areas overlap across the metro area. The provider depends on the address, so confirm it for any home you are considering, along with water, sewer and trash service.

faqs.q: What historic districts are in Phoenix?
faqs.a: Phoenix has 36 residential historic districts with Historic Preservation overlay zoning. Well-known examples include Willo, Encanto-Palmcroft, F.Q. Story, Roosevelt, Coronado, Country Club Park and Windsor Square. Exterior changes in these districts may require review, so ask about the rules before you buy.

Maryvale is an urban village on the west side of Phoenix that began as a planned community by developer John F. Long, who was selling homes there by 1954 and named it after his wife, Mary. Much of its housing is mid-century ranch homes, and the Milwaukee Brewers hold spring training at the ballpark that opened as Maryvale Baseball Park.

Interstate 10 and Interstate 17 meet near downtown. Loop 101 and Loop 202 circle much of the metro area, State Route 51 runs north from downtown, and Loop 303 crosses the far north of the city. Valley Metro operates light rail and buses, and Sky Harbor sits just east of downtown.

Many. Phoenix Union High School District covers much of the older city and works with partner elementary districts such as Alhambra, Cartwright, Isaac, Laveen, Murphy, Osborn and Roosevelt. Other areas are served by other districts. Confirm the assigned schools for any specific address directly with the district.

faqs.q: How do I find my Phoenix home's value?
faqs.a: Ask for a comparative market analysis. Phoenix is too large and varied for a single citywide number, and values swing from one village, street and home to the next. Teigh reviews recent nearby sales and active competition, then explains her recommendation in a no-obligation consultation.
